title: A mirror of political violence: How a far-right activist was killed in Lyon
subhead: Police questioned both left- and right-wing radical activists to retrace what happened the day Quentin Deranque, 23, was killed. Mimetic violence sprang from adrenaline and uncontrolled actions, devastating young people's lives.

subhead: Left-wing MEP Raphaël Glucksmann, a vocal Kremlin critic expected to run for France's top job next year, said that authorities had told him he was targeted by an operation linked to Russian intelligence.

title: 'With arson, they are forced to release students': Kenya's boarding school system nears breaking point
subhead: Since the start of June, 204 schools have been damaged by students, who are protesting against harsh living conditions, run-down facilities and corporal punishment. At the end of May, 16 boarders died in a dormitory fire.

title: 'Nolan's Odyssey is probably one of the most faithful cinematic adaptations of the Homeric text'
subhead: The British-American director's film prompts a nuanced and profound reflection on humanity. In doing so, it brings Homer's work powerfully into dialogue with the present, observes historian Fabien Bièvre-Perrin.

title: The Golden Owl, the treasure hunt that drives you mad: 'No one listens to anyone anymore'
subhead: 'The Golden Owl's last secrets' (1/6). Thirty-one years after it was buried, the treasure known as La Chouette d'Or, or Golden Owl, was discovered on the night of October 2, 2024. Yet, many 'chouetteurs' – the name given to the community of treasure hunters obsessed with this elusive statuette – never stopped searching for 'the real one.' Something doesn't add up.

subhead: For the past year, traditional steam baths from Eastern Europe and Russia have been springing up across the Catalan capital. Popular with both Russians and Ukrainians – who arrived by the thousands on the Costa Brava at the start of the war in 2022 – the establishments have become an unexpected place for the two communities to coexist.

title: Fire in southwest France: Questions raised over management of blaze's first hours
subhead: Now that the megafire that devastated 42,000 hectares in the Gironde department has been brought under control since Saturday, residents of the hardest-hit towns and cities have voiced their anger. Nearly 1,000 of them want a complaint to be filed against persons unknown.
